teams.heading: Jake White confirmed as Fiji head coach, succeeding interim Senirusi Seruvakula
teams.body: Jake White, the 2007 World Cup-winning Springbok coach, has been confirmed as Fiji's head coach, the Fiji Rugby Union announced on Tuesday after a field of 31 applicants. He replaces interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula, and the appointment follows Monday's Fiji Sun report that Warren Gatland, the former Wales and British & Irish Lions coach, was close to the job. White's brief is the 2027 World Cup, and he has said: "Next year is about building depth and, obviously, the last block is to peak before the World Cup."

lead.why: Confirmation of Jake White as head coach is the decisive new development on the story already reported as a tip and a Gatland rumour.

teams.heading: Manny Iyogun signs new Northampton deal, keeping England prop at Franklin's Gardens
teams.body: Manny Iyogun, the Northampton academy product who made his England Test debut off the bench against Argentina in July, has signed a new contract at Franklin's Gardens, extending beyond the current season. The 25-year-old loosehead has 104 senior appearances for Saints and follows Tommy Freeman, Henry Pollock and Tom Pearson in re-signing with the Prem champions. Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson praised him as a brilliant character who embodies the club's values, and Iyogun says staying was an easy decision.

lead.why: A new England Test prop contract is the freshest story with corroboration from both BBC and Planet Rugby, and it touches England's selection pool directly.

teams.heading: Stade Français's Paul Gustard fears Lucas Peyresblanques out five to six months
teams.body: Stade Français have lost hooker Lucas Peyresblanques to a fractured fibula, and coach Paul Gustard says they risk losing him for five to six months. The 27-year-old underwent surgery on Sunday after being cleared out at a breakdown against Montpellier. Gustard also flagged centre Noah Nene, who could be out around two weeks, while the extent of No. 8 Yoan Tanga's rib injury is unclear. SA Rugby Magazine reports the trio are set to miss Saturday's Champions Cup opener at the Bulls.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item reporting a fresh injury and selection consequence, though it concerns a Stade Français club side rather than the France XV.

teams.heading: Rugby brain injury claimants reportedly get reprieve over £2.8m legal bill
teams.body: Players in rugby's brain injury lawsuit have been granted a reprieve, according to a Yahoo Sports report on the case. It follows the Guardian's earlier report that claimants faced a £2.8m legal bill to keep the litigation going. No terms have been reported, so it is unclear whether the fees are settled or how the case now proceeds.

teams.heading: Scotland's best-ever world ranking is No. 5, last reached in 2026
teams.body: No. 5 is the highest men's world ranking Scotland have ever reached. The record lists that position in 2017, across 2017–18, in 2018, in 2023 and in 2026, so it has been a repeated high-water mark rather than a single peak. Those are the only years in the record, and the figure is a ceiling, not a current position.

teams.heading: Kieran Hardy faces knee surgery and months out, missing Wales' autumn Tests
teams.body: Ospreys transition coach Richard Kelly confirmed on Tuesday that Wales scrum-half Kieran Hardy needs knee surgery and faces months, not weeks, on the sidelines. The 32-cap international was helped off in the first half of Friday's 38-31 win at Dragons and had been expected to feature in head coach Steve Tandy's autumn Tests. BBC Sport says he also appears a serious doubt for next year's Six Nations, a development likely to increase calls for former Wales scrum-half Gareth Davies to reverse his retirement.

lead.why: A new injury to a Wales scrum-half that removes him from the autumn Tests, which no earlier edition has covered.

teams.heading: Argentina join Uruguay, Chile and Brazil in joint 2035 World Cup bid
teams.body: Argentina have joined Uruguay, Chile and Brazil in submitting a joint bid to host the 2035 World Cup, with the report surfacing in early October. A shared bid puts the Pumas' ambitions beyond the Nations Championship table and alongside their neighbours, a regional project rather than a solo one. Those ambitions sit against a 24-31 defeat to England in Round 3, which leaves Argentina eighth of 12 in the log.

lead.why: Argentina's own union is part of a joint bid, a new story not yet covered in earlier editions, while the Edwards items were already reported on 11 October.

teams.heading: Mark Nawaqanitawase unavailable for Wallabies' UK tests, weighing Fiji or Italy
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase will not be available for the Wallabies' away Nations Championship Tests against England, Scotland and Wales, his agent Milan Volavola-Shankar told Code Sports. Volavola-Shankar said Nawaqanitawase told Les Kiss, the Wallabies coach, of the decision in July, before he joins the Panasonic Wild Knights in Japan. The 26-year-old qualifies for Fiji through his biological father and is also eligible for Italy, and his three-year stand-down ends in August next year, with any decisions to be considered "at the appropriate time".

lead.why: A fresh availability and eligibility story that affects the Wallabies' UK tour, unlike the earlier pieces already seen.

teams.heading: Kieran Read urges All Blacks consistency for Sydney Bledisloe Test
teams.body: Former All Blacks number eight Kieran Read has argued against changing the starting XV for Saturday's Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney, saying "I'd like to see a consistent team as much as we can." Former All Blacks scrum-half Justin Marshall agreed, saying "there's still too much grey for us to be too experimental". Lock Fabian Holland, who started the first two Springboks Tests before being moved to the bench for the third, has not been included in the last two All Blacks Tests.

lead.why: It is the only new item about All Blacks selection, and it is the storyline a fan would argue about before the Sydney Test.

teams.heading: Wilco Louw dropped from Stormers side for Champions Cup opener against Bristol
teams.body: Springbok prop Wilco Louw has been left out of the Stormers matchday side entirely for the Champions Cup opener against Bristol Bears, with Zachary Porthen named among the replacements. Stormers director of rugby John Dobson made the change after Louw started at tighthead in the 39-22 United Rugby Championship derby win over the Sharks, and pointed to Bristol's high-movement game under Pat Lam as a reason it may not suit him. Sazi Sandi starts at tighthead, while Springbok Evan Roos, back from a hamstring injury, returns at number eight.

lead.why: It is a new Springbok selection story with named players and a clear decision, and it is the only new item in the pack with reported body text.
